keyVerseText: This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.
rootMeaning: The word ἀποδοχή (apodochḗ) derives from the verb ἀποδέχομαι (apodéchomai), which means to accept or receive gladly. This root conveys not merely a passive reception but an active welcoming or approval, indicating a full and willing acceptance. Thus, beyond the general English term 'acceptance,' the root emphasizes a gracious reception and approbation, highlighting relational and intentional aspects of receiving.
usageInScripture: With only two occurrences in the New Testament, ἀποδοχή is consistently translated as 'acceptation,' reflecting a sense of worthy reception or approval. Its limited but focused usage suggests that the term carries a weighty connotation of something being fully embraced or regarded as trustworthy and fitting. This consistency underscores the term's role in expressing not just acceptance but a commendation or endorsement within the scriptural context.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἀποδοχή in its original sense enriches our grasp of Christian faith by emphasizing the wholehearted acceptance and approval that Christ's work merits. The term points to the divine reception of the gospel message as faithful and worthy, inviting believers to respond with trust and confidence. This concept also challenges believers to recognize the depth of God's approval in salvation, which is not casual but deliberate and gracious. Consequently, ἀποδοχή encapsulates the essence of receiving Christ's redemptive work with full assent and joy.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Timothy 1:15, the phrase 'worthy of all acceptation' uses ἀποδοχή to affirm the trustworthy and commendable nature of the statement that Christ Jesus came to save sinners. This word highlights that the message is not only true but deserving of full and willing reception by all believers. It calls the reader to embrace this gospel truth with confidence and reverence, recognizing its supreme value and divine approval.
